title: France and Germany strike deal on car emissions and UK special status
extract: France and Germany have agreed on changes to the EU’s car-emissions approach, including a proposed 90% reduction target that leaves room for compensating measures. The agreement could also give the UK a route into the bloc’s future 'Made in EU' rules, with implications for automakers and supply chains.

title: Calls grow to limit London's rollout of driverless robotaxis
extract: London’s planned robotaxi rollout is drawing objections from drivers and public figures, who want Transport for London to have clear powers to regulate autonomous ride-hailing. The debate puts the practical and employment consequences of self-driving taxis in focus.

title: China proposes tighter export controls on AI technologies
extract: Beijing has proposed export controls covering 23 AI technologies as part of a wider review of strategic technology exports. The draft targets some overseas deployments involving sensitive model technology while proposing to keep ordinary access through APIs, apps and software-as-a-service outside the restrictions.

title: IMF chief warns AI risks could outweigh its benefits without safeguards
extract: IMF managing director Kristalina Georgieva says artificial intelligence could deliver substantial economic gains but also negative shocks if productivity improvements fail to materialise or safeguards are inadequate. Her remarks add to the debate about governance and financial stability as AI adoption accelerates.

title: Anthropic's Jack Clark says AI's impact is accelerating rapidly
extract: Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark says AI capabilities are advancing at an accelerating pace and could have a major effect on US economic output. He also argues that international coordination will be needed to establish rules as increasingly capable systems spread.

title: Many English NHS trusts reject or move away from Palantir patient-data platform
extract: Freedom of information responses show that a number of NHS trusts have declined to use, or have moved away from, the Federated Data Platform supplied by Palantir. Some trusts say it duplicates systems they already have, while others report benefits for scheduling, highlighting the mixed reception for the national programme.

title: New Amiga datatype renders PC ANSI art in the IBM VGA font
extract: The new PC ANSI datatype reads .ans BBS screens and .nfo artwork as text, rendering them with the IBM VGA font and 16 colours. The developer says it has been tested against 1,712 files from the 16colo.rs archive, bringing a distinctive PC-era text-art format to Amiga software.

title: A ZX Spectrum 128K, +2 and +3 emulator is being built for an ESP32-S3 handheld
extract: This project brings a Spectrum 128K, +2 and +3 to a 7-inch ESP32-S3 device, including a cycle-aware Z80 and ULA, AY and beeper audio, tape and disk support, snapshots and Bluetooth keyboard input. It is a substantial modern hardware project focused on reproducing the original machines’ behaviour.

title: Terra Strike brings a Zarch-style 3D landscape shooter to the Amiga
extract: A new 68k Amiga game project takes inspiration from Zarch: pilot over a flat-shaded 3D island, attack tanks, buildings and ships, then land to refuel. The project is developing a distinctly modern homebrew game around the look and feel of classic Amiga-era 3D action.

title: A new megademo recreates C64 and Amiga demo-scene style in JavaScript and Python
extract: This project builds a modern megademo inspired by Commodore 64 and Amiga productions, using JavaScript and Python in Circuitry Studio. It is a contemporary experiment in recreating the form and atmosphere of classic computer demos.

title: The best recent crime and thrillers: review roundup
extract: This roundup surveys new crime and thriller fiction, including Ian Rankin’s The Heights and several mysteries built around family secrets, inheritance and investigation. It offers a useful cross-section of current work in the crime and thriller genres.

title: Tim Jeal obituary: biographer who reshaped views of Victorian explorers
extract: The biographer and novelist Tim Jeal, who has died aged 81, challenged received accounts of figures including Henry Morton Stanley, David Livingstone and Robert Baden-Powell. His work combined historical research with a willingness to question heroic national narratives.

title: From The Shining to Trainspotting: what makes a great film adaptation?
extract: A look at successful adaptations argues that films often work best when they creatively reinterpret their source material rather than reproduce it faithfully. Examples such as The Shining and Children of Men show how directors can preserve a story’s force while making something distinct for the screen.

title: The Face of Horror review: a playful, stylish spin on Hammer horror
extract: Anna Biller’s horror film borrows the flavour of 1960s Hammer while relocating its ghost-story sensibility to medieval Japan. The review praises its playful genre touches, black comedy and striking visual style, describing it as a potential cult favourite.

title: Klara and the Sun review: Taika Waititi's adaptation is a sentimental robot story
extract: Taika Waititi adapts Kazuo Ishiguro’s novel about an artificial friend observing a human family in a near-future world shaped by advanced technology. The review is critical of the film’s tone, but the subject makes it a notable science-fiction adaptation about artificial intelligence and personhood.

title: Look Back review: Kore-eda adapts a manga about friendship and artistic ambition
extract: Hirokazu Kore-eda’s live-action adaptation of Tatsuki Fujimoto’s manga follows two young artists whose friendship is shaped by ambition, collaboration and loss. It brings the manga’s emotional intensity to a film screened at the London Film Festival.

title: Masterplan review: a glossy heist caper with spy-tech gimmicks
extract: Stanley Tucci stars in a heist comedy built around a Louvre robbery and technological tricks including retinal-scan cloning and virtual-reality intrusion. The review finds the caper lightweight, but its mix of espionage, comedy and gadgetry makes it an entertaining genre release to track.

title: Winnie-the-Pooh turns 100 as the character's cultural life continues
extract: A century after A. A. Milne’s first Pooh book, new BBC programmes and commemorations revisit the bear’s history and his place in popular culture. The anniversary is also a reminder of how a literary character became a lasting presence across illustration, animation and merchandise.
